column1: # Every options class that accepts a `@qmx-threshold` override, classified by the
# SHAPE OF THE DECISION its rule then makes. This is the population Ш7's seam —
# "a threshold is a decision, not a number" — must either cover or exclude by name.
#   then, per class: the fields withOverride() assigns, and what getSeverity() does.
# ROW COUNT: 27 classes. 25 decide from one measured value against a pair of
# bounds — the shape a seam can carry. 2 do not, and they are named here rather
#   - DataClassOptions: getSeverity() returns Warning unconditionally, ignoring
#     its argument; the rule compares WOC and WMC separately. The override's two
#     halves are bounds on two DIFFERENT metrics, so "warning" and "error" are
#   - GodClassOptions: getSeverity() is `$value > 0 ? Warning : null`, and its own
#     comment says severity is decided inline in analyze() from matchedCount vs
#     evaluableCount. The override moves `minCriteria`, a count of criteria, and
# WHY THE FIELD NAMES ARE NOT THE CLASSIFIER, stated because the first two
# attempts used them and both were wrong. Six classes spell the pair
# `maxWarning`/`maxError` rather than `warning`/`error`, which a name-based probe
# calls "other" though they are ordinary pairs. And DataClassOptions assigns one
# field from `warning` and one from `error`, which a shape-based probe calls an
# ordinary pair though its two fields bound different measurements. Only reading
# WHAT THIS METHOD DOES NOT SEE
# - Rules that read effective options and compare fields themselves instead of
#   calling getSeverity(): they are the reason the seam is needed, and this table
#   classifies the options, not the call sites. The companion enumeration
# - Whether a rule's own inline comparison agrees with its options class's
#   getSeverity(). For the two exceptions above it demonstrably does not.
